content: The hindgut, also known as the epigaster, represents the posterior (caudal) portion of the alimentary canal. It encompasses the distal third of the transverse colon, the splenic flexure, the descending colon, the sigmoid colon, the rectum, and the upper part of the anal canal. The arterial blood supply to the hindgut is provided by the inferior mesenteric artery. Venous drainage occurs via the portal venous system. Lymphatic drainage is directed to the chyle cistern. The autonomic innervation of the hindgut is mediated through the inferior mesenteric plexus. Sympathetic innervation is derived from the lumbar splanchnic nerves, specifically from spinal levels L1 to L2. Parasympathetic innervation originates from spinal levels S2 to S4. Additional images include depictions of the abdominal portion of the digestive tube and its attachment to the primitive or common mesentery, as well as illustrations of a six-week-old human embryo and the tail end of a human embryo aged twenty-five to twenty-nine days.
